core_obligations: Record that the forward implication is formal (proof line 2225).

For the converse, take a finite purely inseparable extension k''/k with a point x'' above x, choose a common extension field of k' and k'' together with a point above both x' and x'', and identify the map of local rings between the two base changes (proof lines 2226-2234).

Conclude: that map is a flat local homomorphism, hence faithfully flat, the target is normal by hypothesis, so the source is normal by descent of normality, and the pointwise criterion then gives geometric normality of X at x (proof lines 2235-2240).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to finite purely inseparable extensions and pick a common extension (proof lines 2226-2234).
Descend normality along the flat local map (proof lines 2235-2240).
difficulty_reason: For X over k, a field extension k'/k, a point x and a point x' of X_{k'} above it, the lemma shows that geometric normality at x is equivalent to geometric normality at x' over k', with the global statement as a corollary (statement lines 2209-2222). The forward implication is formal. For the converse the author again reduces to the defining condition on finite purely inseparable extensions: given k''/k finite purely inseparable and a point x'' above x, one chooses a common extension field of k' and k'' with a point above both, and observes that the map between the corresponding local rings is a flat local homomorphism, hence faithfully flat; normality upstairs therefore descends to the local ring over k'', and the pointwise criterion gives geometric normality over k (proof lines 2225-2240). The claim is H2: the same reduction pattern as for geometric regularity, with descent of normality along faithfully flat local maps in place of descent of regularity.
